title: First readers, iv
venue: Arthur's site (newspaper cadence: six dailies + a Sunday)
logline: Friday. The counter says 212. Wood draws the number as a crowd and can't; he draws it as a beach and can't; he draws it as 212 stick figures and the panel is black. He erases to twelve and keeps the twelve.

panels.composition: The garage. The CRT: 212. WOOD looking at it.

image.prompt: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, a man at a CRT monitor reading a visitor counter, a small dog beside him

panels.composition: The pad: 212 stick figures. The panel nearly black with them. Illegible.

image.prompt: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, a drawing pad crammed with over two hundred crude stick figures so densely that the page reads as nearly black

panels.composition: Erasing. Two hundred gone. Twelve left, at the back, where they fit.

image.prompt: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, a man erasing a crowded page down to twelve stick figures standing at the back

panels.composition: Wood, to the dog. The twelve behind him.

balloons.text: Twelve. Twelve stands for two hundred and twelve.
That's how it'll work from now on. Twelve is everybody.

image.prompt: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, a man speaking to a small dog with twelve stick figures behind him

art.line: brush-pen scanned; muddy early-digital flats begin
art.palette: limited, muddy; Sundays in over-wet watercolor

notes: 212 erased to twelve. 'Twelve is everybody.' (The chorus's count rule.)
